errorCodes.meaning: `subject` is the administrator issuing the invite. A subject's step-up factor is never bound on the strength of their own signing key — that would let whoever stole the key mint a factor for it.
The relying party does not recognise the subject — it holds no standing a step-up could ever be asked of.
`ttlSeconds` exceeds 24 hours or the relying party's own lower cap. `details.maxTtl` MAY state the cap in seconds.

ApproverLabel.description: A human-readable name for where the approver lives — e.g. `Browser plugin — work laptop`. Chosen by the subject (or suggested by an inviter), untrusted, and attributed to its author wherever it is rendered. Absent rather than invented when none was chosen.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Response.description: The issued invite. The claim code is returned only here.

claimCode.description: A short code (≥40 bits) the invited subject types at redemption, returned exactly once. Delivered by the administrator over a different channel from `url`. The relying party stores only a slow hash of it.

expiresAt.description: When the invite stops being redeemable.

inviteId.description: The relying party's identifier for the invite, for audit and administration. Not a redemption factor: it is neither the token nor derivable from it.

url.description: Where the invited subject redeems the invite. Carries the single-use token (≥128 bits). MUST NOT carry the claim code.

schema.description: An administrator asks the relying party for a single-use invite, redeemed by the invited subject with a separately delivered claim code, to bind a step-up approver to that subject. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

label.description: A suggested label for the approver. The subject MAY override it at redeem/finish.

subject.description: The DID invited to bind a step-up approver. MUST be a subject the relying party recognises, and MUST NOT be the administrator issuing the invite.

ttlSeconds.description: Seconds the invite stays redeemable. Default 900 (15 minutes). The relying party refuses more than 86400 (24 hours), or more than its own lower cap, with `ttlTooLong`.
